title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: When combining multiple models, consider how each model's predictions contribute to the overall prediction. Think about how averaging predictions might affect the bias and variance.

title: Effect on Bias
text: Averaging predictions from multiple models can help reduce the variance of the predictions. However, consider whether this process affects the bias of the model.

title: Effect on Variance
text: When you average predictions from multiple models, the variance of the predictions tends to decrease. This is because the averaging process smooths out the fluctuations in individual model predictions.

hintAnswer: Averaging predictions does not inherently change the bias of the model.
title: Analyzing Bias
text: Consider the definition of bias in the context of model predictions. Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Does averaging predictions from multiple models change this approximation?
choices: Averaging predictions does not inherently change the bias of the model.

hintAnswer: Averaging predictions reduces the variance of the model.
title: Analyzing Variance
text: Variance refers to the variability of model predictions for a given data point. When you average predictions from multiple models, how does this affect the variability of the predictions?
choices: Averaging predictions reduces the variance of the model.
